# Synthetic nullary allocation before constructor delegation

An exact public synthetic nullary initializer creates an original raw callback
before same-owner constructor delegation. The caller retains nested covariant
map arguments, float bits, the new callback identity, the selected overload and
each prefix effect. Four frozen routes compare 96 cases twice with source/SDK
interface declarations. All output compiles; original synthetic class/constructor
bits are restored through exact Code-preserving header edits before the full
identity/metadata and runtime audit. Six wrong programs and six unchanged-Code
Signature controls protect the proof. Only authored fixtures execute.

A separate positive Signature control binds the callback to another already-declared Object-bound owner formal. Its unchanged original Code is decompiled, fully compiled, checked for exact original entries/metadata and compared with the same 96-case runtime baseline. The raw allocation supplies no relation between independent owner formals; an undeclared callback element remains rejected.
